claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
CoCrFeNi has acceptable low-temperature wear but develops increased friction and wear at elevated sliding temperatures.
A minor Ti, Nb, or similar addition to CoCrFeNi will promote nano-coupled grains and nanoscale second-phase precipitates during processing.
The minor addition will create a nanohierarchical architecture with spatial composition undulation in CoCrFeNi.
A nanohierarchical structure containing nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates can provide adaptive friction-interface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified CoCrFeNi will contain ultrafine grains and well-distributed nanoscale precipitates.
During high-temperature sliding, the nanohierarchical microstructure will evolve into an ultra-nanocrystalline glaze layer.
At low temperature, the multiphase nanostructure provides multiple deformation pathways that dissipate or release frictional stress in stages.
At high temperature, nanoscale precipitates coalesce to form the protective glaze layer.
A dense nanocrystalline glaze layer formed at 800 °C minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
The modified material will maintain low friction throughout sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified material will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire temperature range.
The modified material will have at least an order-of-magnitude lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed protection is applicable in ambient or similar industrial environments under service-representative sliding loads.
